ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: the weather, as the colony knows it
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: The colony's own weather record: its records, its seasons remembered by name, and the weather in its people, its visitors and its events.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: The Overview page's Weather card compares this season with the same season last year, and lists the colony's weather records.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: From the day Rimfolk comes, each home map keeps a record of its weather. Once an hour it notes whether rain or snow is falling, whether there is a storm or fog, and how cold or warm it is outside. The hours make days and the days make seasons, and a month of days and three years of seasons are kept. The game still chooses the weather, along with any weather mods; Rimfolk only weighs that choice as the land and the last days make likely, moves the temperature a few degrees with it, and lets someone who reads the weather say what's coming (the settings under "The weather", on the What's on page).

li.heading: Records and seasons

table.li: What | When it counts | What you see
The coldest or hottest since the colony came | After the record has 20 days, and a degree past the mark | A word from someone in view, and the news
The longest rain | Rain most of the day, more days running than any earlier spell of four or more | The same
The longest dry spell | Nothing falling, longer than any earlier spell of a week or more | The same
The first snow | Snow after ten days without, set against last year's first snow | The news, when it came five days or more earlier or later

A season against last year's | 3 °C colder or warmer; three more wet days and half again; or a day's more storms and twice as many | The news and the chronicle, and a journal line from whoever has been with the colony longest

A season remembered by name | 5 °C colder or warmer than usual here, two days of storms, rain on most days, or 12 days running with nothing falling where it usually rains | "the winter of the long cold", "the warm winter", "the dry summer": the news, the chronicle and the year's annals

li.after: The Overview page has a Weather card: this season so far against the same season last year, the records, and the last season remembered by name. The year's annals say how cold and how hot it got.

li.heading: Weather that changes like weather
li.text: When a weather ends, the game chooses the next from the land's own weathers and their weights (Seasonal Weather's by season, and those of any other weather mod). Rimfolk weighs them as the land and the last days make likely, and together the ordinary weathers keep the chance they had: the special ones (a double rainbow, blood rain, acid smog) and anything an event or a weather controller forces are left as they are. Over the years each land keeps about the rain it had, and a desert stays a desert.

table.li: What | How

Spells | A few wet days make rain likelier for a while, until the spell breaks (after 3 days in a dry land, 9 in a humid one, 6 elsewhere). A dry spell holds, and after 8 days (5 in a humid land) breaks with rain, and in the warm with a storm; in a dry land, where long dry spells are usual, it only now and then breaks with a storm, after 12. Snow keeps falling for a few days, then clears.

What follows what | Clouds build into rain and a storm settles into rain. A storm seldom comes out of a clear sky, except on a hot afternoon or along a cold front. Fog comes after a cold clear night or rain, more over open water, and seldom in the wind. A cold front (a day 5 °C or more colder than the one before) brings snow, or a storm where it's still warm, then clear skies; stronger where summers are hot and winters cold.

Events and conditions | The long rains bring more rain for five days, a growing spell soft rain without storms, high water and a thirsty herd drier days, an ice fair settled cold, and the sky clears after hail. A heat wave, a warm spell, a cold snap and Stormproof's heat dome and polar front bring clear skies. Any drought (the region's, the game's or Vanilla Events Expanded's) means less rain and never more; the region's hard winter brings more snow and its floods more rain.

The year | Each year leans a little wetter or drier, and a dry land's years vary more. The annals say a year was wet or dry against the years before it, and warm or cold against the land's usual, once it was.

Seasons | Where Seasonal Weather gives the land its seasons, or the land is always frozen, they are left as they are. A tropical land it doesn't cover has a wet season of two quadrums and a dry one; elsewhere storms come in summer and few in winter, with a little more rain in spring and fall.
Fog | A fog in the night or the morning lifts by late morning; one by day passes in a few hours. On land that's always frozen, fog lasts as the game has it.

Temperature | Up to 3 °C cooler under rain on a warm day, a degree more in a storm; colder on a clear night (twice as much in a dry land, less in a humid one, more over snow); milder under cloud, fog or rain at night; a little warmer in clear sunshine; colder over snow cover. Each year leans about a degree warmer or colder at most. Never more than 5 °C down or 3 °C up, eased in over a couple of hours.

Forecasts | A few hours before the weather changes, the colonist who reads it best (Plants 6, or 3 for an older hand) says what's coming if they're in view, and the Overview's Weather card shows it. What comes is held to unless it can no longer come. The forecast is right seven times in ten for a fair hand and up to nine for an old hand; with a weather station from Stormproof or Weather Control it's nearly always right. Whoever got it wrong may own up to it. While someone whose body sets the weather is on the map (Alpha Genes' rainmaker and the like, a colonist or a stranger), nobody foretells it.

li.after: Only on home maps with weather of their own (not in space or a pocket map). Each part has its own setting, and all need the deeper game hooks. Nothing is added to the map: switching them off, or taking Rimfolk out, leaves the game's own weather.

li.heading: Seasons with a character of their own
li.text: Each season gets a character when it begins, drawn from the land's climate and the year: the same land and year always give the same seasons. About half the seasons are ordinary. The rest lean one way: wet or dry, warm or cold, and where snow is what falls (a season whose usual mean is 3 °C or less) snowy or short of snow. About one season in ten is extreme. The rain and snow lean the weather the game chooses (with "Weather that changes like weather"), so a season only brings more or less of the weathers the land already has; the temperature moves for the whole season, eased in over about half a day. At the start of each season the colonist who reads the weather best says what kind of season it looks like, over their head if they are in view, and the news has it; they are right a little less often than about tomorrow's weather. An extreme season is told once the land shows it: a warm or cold one a day in, a wet, dry or snowy one from its fifth day if the days so far agree.

table.li: Season | Rain and snow | Temperature
Wet | Rain about half again as often (less where it already rains on most days), clear skies less; a very wet one rains about twice as often | Half a degree cooler in summer
Dry | Rain about half as often, more dust and dry storms; a very dry one about a quarter as often | Up to 1 °C warmer in spring and summer, up to 2 °C in a very dry one
Warm | As usual | 2 to 3.5 °C warmer; a hot summer or a very mild winter 4 to 6.5 °C
Cold | As usual | 2 to 3.5 °C colder; a hard winter or a very cold season 4 to 8 °C
Snowy | Snow more often; a winter of deep snow about twice as often | 1 °C colder, 2.5 °C in deep snow
Short of snow | Snow less than half as often, almost none in an extreme | 1 °C milder, 2.5 °C in an extreme

li.after: The setting "The land's climate" (What's on page, under "The weather") makes it gentle (seven seasons in ten ordinary, the rest milder), as designed, or dramatic (a third ordinary, the rest stronger and more often extreme), or switches it off.

li.heading: A year's extremes, and once in a lifetime
li.text: Now and then a year has its own extreme, about one year in twelve as designed: a year without a summer (spring and fall 2.5 to 3.5 °C colder, the summer 4 to 6 °C), a dry year (every season dry, the summer very dry), or a year of heavy rain (spring and fall very wet, the summer wet). The region's world event to match is started where it can be (a year without a summer, the region's drought, its floods, and a hard winter for a hard winter), so the neighbours' news says what the land shows. While those world events run the land feels them too: a year without a summer 3 °C colder, a hard winter 2.5 °C colder, the region's drought a degree warmer in spring and summer. Very rarely, about once in twenty years as designed, a season brings weather from outside the land's own climate for a few days, with the temperature to match, only where the land's own climate never brings it.

table.li: Once in a lifetime | Where and when | How long
Snow | Land where snow never falls (its coldest month 7 °C or more), in its coldest season, taken down to a mean of -6 °C | 2 to 4 days
A hard frost | Warm land (its coldest month 12 °C or more), in its coldest season, down to a mean of 2 °C with frost at night | 3 to 5 days
A great heat | Cold land (its warmest month 16 °C or less), in its warmest season, up to 18 °C warmer | 3 to 6 days
A blizzard | Land with cold winters (its coldest month between -15 and 3 °C) where no blizzard comes (Odyssey's blizzard) | 1.5 to 3 days
A dust storm | Land that isn't wet and has no dust weather, in its warm seasons (Odyssey's sandstorm, else Vanilla Landmarks Expanded's or Seasonal Weather's dust) | 1 to 2 days
Heavy rain | Dry land with no downpour among its weathers (Odyssey's torrential rain, else a thunderstorm) | 1 to 2 days
A great storm | Wet, warm land by open water (Vanilla Psycasts Expanded's hurricane), only within the shared harm budget | About a day

li.after: It is told when it shows (its weather begun, or the cold or heat most of the way in), the chronicle keeps it, a believer may say whose sign they take it for, and the year's annals remember it. As designed it never takes the temperature more than 22 °C down or 18 °C up (16 and 13 gentle, 26 and 22 dramatic).

li.heading: Weathers that come by no biome
li.text: About 25 of the game's and the mods' weathers come only by an event or a psycast. The seasons give some of them a place, each only with its mod: fertile rain in a wet spring or summer (Vanilla Landmarks Expanded's own condition, so the plants grow faster while it lasts), a drizzle in a wet season (ReGrowth), dust in a dry season (Seasonal Weather, Vanilla Landmarks Expanded), fog snow in a snowy winter (Seasonal Weather), a whiteout in a hard or deep-snow winter and swelter in a hot summer (Vanilla Events Expanded), a petal storm (Alpha Biomes) or a double rainbow (Seasonal Weather) in spring, and a fog storm in a wet or cold fall (ReGrowth). Red rain (Alpha Biomes) now and then falls in the last days of a season before a hard one, and some take it as a sign. The region's drought brings a day of dust, its hard winter a whiteout or fog snow. A volcanic winter brings a few hours of ash in the air (Alpha Biomes) and now and then Alpha Biomes' acid rain with its own letter, within the shared harm budget. Blood rain, the death pall, psychic rain, the long night, the inferno and the psycasts' and space's weathers are never brought: they belong to their own events.

li.heading: A climate that drifts
li.text: Over the years the land's climate drifts slowly, one way for the whole game: by 1 to 3 °C a decade as designed and 4 °C in all (about 1 °C a decade and 2.5 °C in all gentle, 2 to 4 °C a decade and 6 °C in all dramatic), and the rain by up to a third more or less. The setting "Climate drift" picks the way: random by the world, warmer, colder, drier or wetter, or off. Unless it is off, a volcanic winter cools the land by 1.5 °C for a few years, a comet sets the climate moving about a degree one way or the other for a few years, the colony's pollution warms its own land (up to 2 °C), and once more than a sixth of the map's trees are gone since the record began, the land is a little warmer and drier. Growing seasons lengthen or shorten and the snow comes earlier or later with it.

li.heading: The land's record
li.text: Each year's weather goes into the land's record: how far from the usual its winter and its summer ran, its wet days, its growing days and the day of its first snow, forty years at most. The year's annals say the year's own extreme, its seasons that had a character and showed it ("The spring was wet and the winter was hard."), once in a lifetime, and, once the record has four years, what it shows since the colony came: "The winters are milder than when the colony came, by about 2 °C." Early in a season the colony's elder (fifty or older, or three years with the colony) says so when it fits the season. The Overview's Weather card shows the season's forecast, once in a lifetime while it lasts, and what the record shows.

li.heading: After a disaster
li.text: When a disaster is over and the land is quiet again, the one best at the work and three others set to it together, with the game's own jobs, if there is anything to do. The chronicle writes it down once they've done some of it, and the year's annals count each disaster ("The earth shook twice, and hail fell on the fields once.").

table.li: Disaster | Who leads | What they do

An earthquake (Seasonal Weather's, or Vanilla Events Expanded's) | The best builder | Go round the roofs and walls: mend what is damaged, rebuild what the game has marked for it, patch the roofs, clean up and haul
A tornado (the game's own, which Vanilla Landmarks Expanded's tornado alley sends) | The best builder | The same, the debris cleared

A flashstorm | The best grower | Once its fires are out in the home area: the burnt trees there and in the fields marked for cutting and cut, the ash cleaned, and the fields sown again where the season allows
Rimfolk's hail | The best grower | Sow again where it flattened the young crops (the hail destroys those outright), and bring in what is ripe
A flood (Odyssey's seasonal flood, Vanilla Landmarks Expanded's tidal flooding) | The best builder | Carry what the water left lying about back to the stores, and clean up

li.after: Nothing damaged, burnt, flattened or left lying about: no party. A party waits while raiders are on the map, and is let go after two days. With "Answers play out on the map" off, nothing is set going.

li.heading: Last winter, remembered
li.text: The record also counts, each season, how many days were too cold for anything to grow (below 6 °C on average, the advisor's own measure of winter), how many stayed below freezing all day, and how many the snow lay on most of the open land. Once it has kept a year of them, the advisor's notes on firewood, the winter stores, the herd's feed and the herd in the cold each add a sentence about last winter here: "Last winter the cold here lasted 19 days, and the coldest night was -24 °C; at today's fires the wood in store lasts 11 such days." The herd's autumn count sets the hay against the same number. Seasons kept before this was counted are left out, so in an older colony it starts a year after the update.

li.heading: Events that speak of the weather
li.text: Rimfolk's events that speak of the weather only come after that weather. The long rains need rain on four of the last seven days. A flush of mushrooms needs a wet day in the last three, a desert bloom one in the last week, and a growing spell two in the last week. A struck tree needs a storm in the last day. Fall's high water and a rockslide in summer or fall need three wet days in the last week. A thirsty herd needs six days with nothing falling here, and an ice fair five days of the last seven below freezing all day. Until the record has that many days, after Rimfolk is first added, these events wait.

li.heading: Seen coming
li.text: Rimfolk's hail is seen coming. For two hours the sky turns green and the wind drops. The colonist who knows the fields best says so if they're in view, and a few others bring in the ripe crops from the open fields. Then the hail comes. It rains with the hail only while it's warm enough to rain, and a rain the hail brought doesn't run on for a day or two after it. When a warm spell sets in, someone outside feels the wind turn.

li.heading: Rain on the yard
li.text: The game already lets rain wash some filth off the open ground: blood, dirt, vomit and the like. Rimfolk makes it go faster the harder it rains, so a day of steady rain leaves the yard clean of most of it. A drizzle adds nothing, rubble and other filth that rain doesn't wash stay where they are, and nothing under a roof is touched. The setting "Rain washes the yard" (What's on page, under "The weather") turns it off.

li.heading: The land over the seasons
li.text: The land of each home map changes with what happens on it and with the season, in four small passes a day. The growing days it counts are those the weather record kept at 6 °C or more on average; winter doesn't count.

points.li: Burnt and felled ground comes back: a burn of a dozen plants or more, six trees or more the colony felled close together outside its fields, three trees a wilt killed or ten grasses a rust killed. Grass comes up after 2 growing days, brush after 12, young trees of the kind that stood there after 25 (after a wilt, of other kinds), and woods after 60; where no wood stood, it is grass and brush again after 25. A few of the land's own plants are set a day on the bare ground, never in the home area, a zone, on a floor, under a roof or next to a building. Each stage is in the news and the woods back in the chronicle; a felled wood grown back is told to the Mossborn, who think better of the colony for it (3 goodwill).

A pasture grazed bare: where the colony's grazing animals crowd a stretch of 16 by 16 cells and the grass covers under a third of the good ground on six days, a few bare cells a day wear to packed earth (rich soil to soil, marshy ground to mud), a quarter of the good ground at most. Rested 20 growing days, the worn ground comes back as it was.

A sickness of the wild plants: about once in 90 growing days, three times as often while the region has a blight and half again in a wet, warm spell; not in a colony's first 20 days, nor within 30 days of the last, and one at a time. A wilt in wild trees of one kind, a rust in the grass, or a rot in the wild berry bushes, with the game's blighted look; a wilting tree stands bare after 2 days. Each growing day it reaches a few more of its kind nearby (more after rain for the rust and the rot; up to 40 trees, 140 grasses or 20 bushes in all), and a sick plant dies after 10 days (a tree), 5 (a grass) or 7 (a bush). With 30 grasses sick, a few wild grazers move off the land. It ends when nothing sick is left, after 45 days, or after 3 cold days, and those still sick pull through.

Water that rises and falls: after four days of a dry spell or a wet one, by the weather record (wet days against the land's usual rain, a dry run of 10 days, a drought or the region's floods). Shallow still water and marsh dry at the edge to mud, then soil, up to 3 cells in; in a wet spell the open ground beside them turns to mud and then marsh, up to 2 cells out, never into the home area, a zone, a floor or within 2 cells of a building. What one spell left goes back first when the other comes, and slowly as usual. A shrunk pond holds no more fish than it can, and a filled one gains a few (Odyssey's fish, which Vanilla Fishing Expanded uses).

li.after: When a sickness has a few plants, the council is asked: cut out the sick and those beside them (marked for cutting, and the best grower and two others set to it), burn it out (on the first dry daylight hour one of the colony walks to a sick plant at least 15 cells from the colony's buildings, fields and home area and sets fire to it; the fire is the game's from there), or let it run. A believer may take a sickness, or a wood grown back, for a god's doing, and say so. A sick wild tree felled is not held against the colony in the Mossborn's ledger. Rivers, the sea and hot springs are never moved: that is left to mods like Living Waters and Waves. Each part has its own setting under "The land" on the What's on page; the sickness needs the deeper game hooks. Switched off, the water goes back to its own edge.

li.heading: The weather in people

points.li: Three quirks: loves the snow (+3 while snow falls; stands out in it in their free time), follows the sun (+3 in sunshine out of doors, grows out of time outdoors and never comes to an undergrounder; sits in the sun), and sleeps best in rain (+3 with rain on the roof, in bed or indoors at night).

On a bitter morning, or any time it's below -15 °C, breath shows at the mouths of colonists outside. Steam rises off the colony's fires out in the open in the cold, and off the sauna's door on a freezing day.
One who dreads storms flinches at each lightning flash and now and then says so. Anyone within a few steps of a strike flinches too.

li.after: All of these need the "visual and sound touches" setting, and the free-time habits need "Small habits".

li.heading: Visitors and missions
li.text: A trade caravan whose stay is nearly over when a storm or a heavy snow sets in waits it out, half a day longer at its spot, once a visit. When the land is snowbound (deep snow on the ground, or snow on most of the last three days), people coming to the colony for a mission take half again as long on their way, and the mission's time is longer by as much. A camp comes dressed and pitched for its weather, and packs up only when the weather would hurt most of them, it grows really extreme, or the air turns poisonous (toxic fallout, a volcanic winter, a flashstorm, noxious haze).

li.heading: Other weather mods

table.li: Mod | What Rimfolk does with it

Seasonal Weather | On a dry, windy day in summer or fall, with grass and brush up to the home area, the advisor suggests a firebreak, and one button marks the brush in a strip 3 cells wide round the home area for cutting. After an earthquake the best builder and a few others go round the roofs and walls (see "After a disaster"); the chronicle remembers it and the annals count the quakes.
Stormproof | The heat dome and the polar front are talked about like a heat wave and a cold snap. All five of its storms send a camp on its way and are in the advisor's "what's happening now".
Weather is kinda cozy | One who loves the rain never comes to dread storms.
SS Lightning Rod | A strike drawn down by a rod gets a word from someone in view.
Disasters: Tornado | A tornado crossing the land goes in the chronicle, someone writes about it once it has passed, and the builders clear up after it.

Vanilla Events Expanded, Vanilla Landmarks Expanded | After Vanilla Events Expanded's earthquake, and after Vanilla Landmarks Expanded's tidal flooding and the tornadoes of its tornado alley, the colony clears up as after the others.
Quiet Wonders | Rimfolk's firefly nights leave the fireflies to it.

li.after: Each only with its mod, and all of them are safe to add to a running save.
